newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK OTE PICKS NARROWS FIELD OF MOBILE TELE FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK OTE PICKS NARROWS FIELD OF MOBILE TELE FIRMS.

text.p: Greece's telecom organisation OTE has approved a short list of international firms for its strategic partner in the development of the DCS-1800 mobile phone system in Greece, it said in a statement.
The evaluation of the firms to be included in the short list was carried out by its advisors, CS First Boston and Greek Alpha Finance.
The two existing GSM mobile phone operators, Telestet and Panafon, have taken OTE to the state council saying they were awarded a monopoly for eight years and trying to block the OTE system.
The firms short-listed by OTE were:

U.S Airtour International, BellSouth Europe belonging to U.S BellSouth, French Bouygues operating a DCS-1800 system in France, Mannesmann Europe, British Orange holding the fourth DCS-1800 licence belonging to Hutchison Whampoa Group, SBC Communications, Swiss PTT operating a combined mobile network of GSM and DCS-1800 in Switzerland, Tele Denmark and Norwegian Telenor.
Germany's Debitel, Korea Mobile telecom, Kuwait mobile telecom, U.S Motorola, NTT/Itochu Telesystem and U.S. International Wireless had also expressed interest until September 16, it said.
OTE's board of directors also decided to participate in the international consortium Zephir SA that took part in the Romanian government's tender for two mobile telephony GSM licences, it said.
Telenor, Tele Denmark, U.S Motorola and 11 Romanian companies make up the consortium.

OTE will have a 10 percent stake in Zephir SA and the total investment outlay is estimated at $400 million. The GSM licence is expected to be good for more than a decade, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
